Which actor played a villain role too well for comfort? Ann Dowd as Joan in Hereditary. ***Spoiler Alert*** The performance by this relatively unknown actress blew me away and everyone who I've known to watch this film. Joan is the motherly figure who befriends Toni Collette's main character Annie who is going through a really tough time. Toni Collette's exemplary performance as a depressed middle aged mother suffering from tragedy is complimented by Ann Dowd's Joan who wins the heart of the viewers as a sympathetic, patient and caring matriarchal figure in the first half, only to suddenly transform into someone truly terrifying in the second half. What was scary for me about her performance was the genuine warmth she generated from the very moment she entered the screen. I can't see anyone being unable to put their guard down and love and accept this lady. It didn't seem like a performance at all. It seemed like that is how Ann Dowd really is. However when she lifts the veil it is almost bloodcurdling to see the transformation in her appearance and especially in her voice. Nothing is more scarier to me than evil people convincingly disguised as good and with that Ann Dowd truly delivered.

Have you ever sabotaged food because someone was stealing it? Is it possible to sabotage someone's lunch by accident? Yes it is. I was the saboteur. The idiot saboteur. Summer was a co-worker of mine at a warehouse I was employed in during my early adulthood. She was a nice girl but she would often get entangled in workplace drama with other provocative and emotional females likes herself. Things got so bad with her that her enemies would go to extreme lengths to sully her reputation or cause harm e.g. calling her boyfriend at night using a private number, spread nasty rumors (some turned out to be true) about her amongst her closest workmates. To work in such an environment could make any girl a little paranoid. Summer was no exception. One faithful afternoon I was about to enjoy my lunch in our staff lunch room. Lunch times were staggered at 12–1pm for some 1–2pm for the rest. I would normally take my lunch at 12pm while Summer took hers afterwards at 1pm. I collected my lunch in the staff fridge and heated it in the microwave. I joined my friends in the 'mess hall’ where we proceeded to have a very exciting conversation about what crap to do with our money when we got paid. While tearing into a chicken drumstick someone made a comment that my mother prepared a really nice lunch for me today. I took a good look down at my lunch bowl and my heart sank. This wasn't my lunch! It was the exact same bowl like mine…..with an orange cover, a little better kept though…..but this was someone else's lunch! I tried to keep my cool. I told my friends I needed to reheat my lunch. Scared to death I would chance upon the true owner coming towards the kitchen, spotting me carrying his/her lunch like a bloody beggar-thief I haphazardly threw the lunch back into the fridge and took out mine. I heated it and returned to my friends like a nervous wreck but eliciting no suspicions. An hour later I'm busy at work when a stern voice comes over the loudspeaker. 'Will all members of staff please report to the kitchen area?’ My heart leaped like stallion in heat. This is it. The s**t has hit the fan. My friends ambled towards me all curious-like saying stuff like 'What the hell is this about?’ and 'Hey, you saw Summer come out from the manager's office in tears? What's her problem now?’ I tried to play it cool but did a terrible job. 'Huh? What da f**k's going on? I got an order to finish. This is bulls**t. Summer is a ho.’ It's a wonder none of them suspected me right then and there. For all staff to be called to a meeting at once meant that this was pretty serious. Somebody's gonna get sent home. My hands started trembling. The warehouse director took center stage and with a wary look on her face explained that Summer had just gone to have her lunch when she observed that it was severely tampered with. She explained that the person tampered with the lunch in such an extreme manner as if to send an insulting, threatening message to her. The director asked that whomsoever did such an act to please reveal him/herself. All the while I stood looking like this: While everyone else around me started to giggle quietly. Summer who stood next to the director stared at me and I immediately looked away. No one came forward. The director gave Summer money to buy lunch. Case dismissed. As we headed back to our respective positions my friends made light banter about the situation. 'We have a food molester at the warehouse. Anyone of us could be the dreaded food molester.’ They then began to laugh. That became a running joke in the warehouse. Twenty minutes later Summer comes towards me and I start to quiver like jelly. 'You see anybody with an orange cover bowl when you were at lunch Elijah?’ I shook my head in the negative. 'Sick f**king people we have working here,’ she continued. 'Yeah.' I said flatly, 'Hmmm.’ 'I mean,’ she continued while raising her voice, 'Interfering with my food? If that person has a problem with me I don't care what they say to my face but to know that some nasty sonofab**ch will go so low…….I mean……. it's just sad…….a sad, sick person.’ 'Yeah.' I replied flatly, 'Boy!……..Hmmm.’ She then stared at me like she did during the meeting. 'Elijah. It was you?’ I feigned a laugh and acted as though it was a joke, 'Yeah. It was me. Who cooked that food girl? Taste real good.’ She smiled and shook her head and went her way. I knew that she suspected the culprit to be a female so I was off the hook. Some years later I am employed elsewhere and I encounter Summer on Facebook. After a brief chat I admitted to her that I was the food molesting culprit. She laughed and said she knew. I asked her how did she know. She said that she found out after the meeting that I had a bowl exactly like hers. She had put 1+1 together. I said, 'So that whole time you spoke to me after the meeting. You knew?’ She said yes. She was playing along with me to judge whether I tampered with her food by accident, as she suspected, or if one of her enemies made me do it……..that my dumb reaction to her comments had said it all. ‘……..It tasted really good though,' was all I could think of saying. Lesson learned: When you tamper with a co-worker's food by accident, it's a good idea to go tell them.

What are the cleverest scams you have come across? Take a breath, grab a coffee if you may, and allow me to explain to you why we are called 'Tricky-dadians’ by the rest of the Caribbean. Band Ladies Around 2016 — 2018 a phenomenon occurred where sightings of these cultish ladies in heavy clothing similar to that of traditional Amish females were found throughout Trinidad. They were typically spotted at commercial areas such as malls and PriceSmarts (Costco) mostly at the parking lot. They were renowned for asking for your assistance with the rebuilding of their church. They claimed to do this with the purchase of their cheap rubber hand bands of which they would charge anything upwards of $20TT. If you refused to buy their generic, overpriced bands they would then initiate Phase 2 of their scheme which would be to overwhelm the victim with guilt with a pathos laden statement of 'Or maybe you could contribute just a small donation. Anything?’ They employed great acting skills and for many, seeing these harmless women in humble, old fashioned garb being constantly refused and rejected for their worthy cause tugged a few heartstrings. However, as with most scams, they got too greedy too fast. Their monthly appearances soon turned to weekly and then daily. Rather than target one location for the day and wrap up afterwards, it soon became clear that they began employing routes. A typical Band Lady route would be PriceSmart Chaguanas till 2pm, Trincity Mall until 6pm and PriceSmart Mausica until 9pm. They were noticed and mentioned by some of the populace but being that they were always pleasant and took 'no’ graciously, no one bothered to think twice about their scheme. However, the last straw was a rather desperate appearance at a CPL T20 cricket match (above photograph). Trinidad is very tolerant of beggars and we throw a blind eye towards scammers for the most part but for the Band Ladies, plying their scheme in the middle of a regional cricket match where national pride was at a peak, created an online outcry. Everyone suddenly posted a story, photo or recording of a dubious encounter with one of these Band Ladies and from that moment on they were no longer seen in public. Warning *Foul language*

What are some inaccuracies or criticisms of JD Vance's book "Hillbilly Elegy"? Oh here we go again. So I'm supposed to assume this has nothing to do with the fact that Trump just appointed JD Vance as his running mate for Vice President. No. The person who asked the question is genuinely interested in a review of Vance's book and the question is in no way a negatively leading question. I haven't read the book yet but I saw the movie. I remember the movie was thrashed by critics and Hollywood acted as though Amy Adams should be drawn and quartered for taking part in such political, propagandist rubbish. The criticism was non stop. I almost believed what the media was saying. Then I watched it and was surprised to discover that it was a really good movie. It was just a simple story about a guy who struggled in life with poverty and drugs in his family and managed to make something of himself thanks to the two people who supported him in his life. The performances were excellent, particularly Amy Adams and Glenn Close and there was nothing remotely political or propagandist about the story. There is nothing in the book that merits me investigating the inaccuracies in the book. It is a memoir. Vance doesn't make any fantastic claims. It's not like Catch Me if You Can or My Wicked Wicked Ways. Did he exaggerate? Did his mother really overdose on heroin or was she just taking a nap? Is Vance's wife really of Indian descent or just three quarters Indian? Did Vance really drive all night to a job interview right after wrestling a heroin needle from his mother or did he just have a stern argument with her, took a nap and a plane the next morning? Does that matter? Are these the ‘inaccuracies’ that should make us condemn the book and Vance? It's astonishing how much the modern left have idealised themselves into believing that they are the final say in regards to everything. That they are never wrong. Any other opinions are stupid, racist or sexist. As a Trinidadian I sometimes argue with such people as to the reality of what goes on on in my country. People who've never even set foot in the country. When will they realize that the more arrogant they behave and the more they tell people what they ought to believe, think, say and feel, the more people will become disenchanted and start doing the opposite of what they suggest. I'm certain Vance's book and the film will see a surge in sales and streaming in the upcoming weeks. I might even come around to reading it, simply because so many critics angrily claim that I shouldn't.

What's the biggest anticlimax in movie history? Bird Box (2018) was throughly gripping. All the characters were well fleshed out and relatable and as ridiculous as the premise was (unseen, omnipresent entities that makes one commit suicide if seen) the suspense and horror was so effective it became the most streamed Netflix film at the time, mostly due to word of mouth. SPOILER ALERT But by God what a stupid ending. After so much trauma in the first half of the film, years later Sandra Bullock’s character Malorie and her children (one biological, one adopted) are rowing blindfolded down a dangerous river to find the people who sent her a transmission as to a safe location. After a nail biting odyssey down the river we are all expecting to be given answers when she finally arrives at this mysterious, resistance base. What are those creatures? Where did they come from? What do they want? Why do people kill themselves just by looking at them? What is the state of the world right now? Do the entities have a weakness, is it possible to fight back? Instead the movie does the most dirty tactic that a studio could possible do. Instead of providing the audience what they waited for and dedicated our energy and emotions toward (answers) the studio goes the cheap route and decides to end the film by answering nothing, leaving the film open to sequels and prequels. This is a trend I’ve noticed in a lot of modern horrors and thrillers. They just can't end the effing movie and give us the closure that we waited two hours for. Ranting aside, Malorie reaches the destination, a school for the blind and everyone assures her that everything will be ok in one of the most corniest and cliched endings ever conceived. It’s a pity Malorie didn’t wake up from a dream and see all the familiar faces around her while uttering ‘There’s no place like home.’ I would’ve much appreciated that ending than the actual ending of Bird Box.

Why do some people not like Coldplay? As probably the only guy answering this question who actually likes Coldplay I’d like to put forward my theory. There are actually two Coldplays. Old Coldplay Modern Coldplay What is the first thing you noticed about the photos? Old Coldplay shows a young band full of awkward post A-Level graduates who don’t care how geeky they look but seem to enjoy each other’s company and being themselves. Modern Coldplay shows an intensely edited photo of four men who are trying their utmost best to look cool and serious. Everything about the photo screams over saturated, highly commercial and bloated. I sincerely doubt the guys even posed together for the photo but rather had separate photos, photoshopped together. Old Coldplay is alternative rock. Yes they wrote a fair share of ballads. Yes they could be whiny, moody and (as another Quora writer has so artfully suggested) ‘sangfroid’ but there was a meticulous attention to instrumentation and songwriting that you can’t listen to songs like Trouble, Clocks and Shiver and call it pop music. They were definitely popular but they weren’t pop. They wrote intelligent songs but with a fair share of technical bravado on their instruments and innovative yet tasteful sound engineering in the same vein of bands like Radiohead and Doves at the time. All old school Coldplay fans would probably share similar sentiments. Us Coldplay fans looked a lot similar to this when we were growing up. Modern Coldplay is an example of commercial pop music at its worst. Take away the sonic instrumental experimentation and instead put in electronic computer programmer loops and samples. Focus more on marketing, publicity and touring rather than on songwriting, innovation and simple band practicing. Throw in a bunch of cringey, force fed collaborations. Envision a basic formula for their craft and then multiply that formula by 300%. (Studio execs: ‘They’re a bit whiny. Let’s make that lead singer go Ohhh ohh ooo every five seconds. That's what the fans seem to like. And let ‘em write a a shitload of slow piano driven ballads. I think they're a woman's rock band. Let them have that guitar player repeating the same derivative chiming hook. In fact toss one of his hooks into the looping software and we'll rework it for an entire album. How about we let each one of them wear a different color? You know like the Spice Girls. Make it seem like they care about stuff around the world like climate change and fair trade and all that crap.’) This is what a modern day Coldplay fan kinda looks like. And that’s why some people don’t like Coldplay. In my humble opinion.

Why is a bronze medal winner happier than a silver medal winner? What is counterfactual thinking? Imagine Jimmy watching the lottery results live on television. 30 (Nice) 23 (Heyy!) 6 (Heyyyy!) 5 (Oh my God!) 8 (Oh my ****** God!) Jumps off couch And the final number… 33 (Nooooooooo. 33! Who the **** plays 33? It's 27. No. No.No.) Falls back onto the couch sobbing. Jimmy got 5 out of the 6 numbers correct. He is rewarded with one tenth of the grand cash prize. Jimmy is heartbroken. All his life he's waited for that moment. All his life he's played the National Lottery dreaming of the day. It was supposed to be today. He feels as though he wants to die. Better he had gotten zilch and saved himself this torment. Freddie is on his security shift. He hears on the radio that one person has won the grand prize. Some people have all the luck. He remembers he bought a ticket and checks to see if he scraped anything. He’s astonished to see that he got 4 out of 6 numbers correct. He got an entire year's salary through sheer luck. He is overjoyed. Far more overjoyed than Jimmy who got ten times his winnings. Moral of the story is that second place winners tend to feel overwhelming disappointment that they were so close to winning while third place winners tend to be happy that they at least got something.

What is the strangest complaint you have received at your job? Some years ago while counting down the last few minutes before my shift ended in a public library, a young woman came to the information desk with an ennraged look on her face. Lady: Can someone please tell me where the Spanish classes are? I've been on all the floors and no one seems to know what I'm talking about. Me: Sorry miss but those aren't Spanish classes. The Spanish Embassy has been having a series of public talks every Wednesday at 5 - 6 pm on the third floor discussing the Latin American economy. We simply allow them to use our conference room on the third floor. Lady: Are you listening to what I'm saying? I left work early to come to these Spanish classes. Where are the people for the Spanish class? Me: I'm sorry miss but we really don't know. We simply give the Embassy access to our conference room. You might want to call the number they left on the advertisement. Lady: So you're saying this is your library, where you work, but you have no idea what's going on? Me: We know all what is going on in regards to our public services but the Embassy's program is something external. Any complaints about the program can be addressed to the Embassy's website. Lady: Typical lazy government worker mentality…So you're saying you have no knowledge of what is going on in your own building? Me: This is actually not our building. Several government departments are housed in this building besides the library. Would you like me to call the Embassy for you? Lady: You've wasted my time already. It's already 5:30pm. I mean does it feel good to you to be getting paid for nothing? What's the point of this library? I want to speak to your manager. I was about to explain to her that we don't have ‘managers’ but librarians when she whips out her cell phone and shows a screenshot of a Facebook post advertising the Embassy's program. Me: Miss. I'm sorry but that post shows that the program ends April 24th, which was two weeks ago… Lady: ……so you….this is so unprofessional…..a big freaking library and you can't call people and tell them that the Spanish class program has finished. I want to speak to the manager. This is unacceptable. It was at this point I decided I that I no longer waste my time with this lady's nonsensical complaint.

What are the things no one tells you about living alone? That it gradually transforms you into someone who WANTS to be alone. If you are like me and have just a drop of introvert blood in you, living alone becomes like an introvert blood transfusion. Or, as I like to call it, an introversion. When you're accustomed hanging out with groups of diverse friends, hearing about the different lifestyles , perceptions and life choices of others, not only does empathy and understanding come naturally but also a desire to empathize and understand people around you grows. If you don't do this regularly, you feel awkward and incomplete. It becomes a subconscious necessity the same way people who have a gym routine tend to always have to be at the gym otherwise they'll be in an awful mood. When you live with someone your mind gravitates towards the study and understanding of the person/persons living with you. Whether it be your spouse, children, sibling, in-law, friend, roommate etc, you naturally become preoccupied studying such an individual and the gears of human nature are in motion in that you become naturally interested in people as a whole. When you live alone, your mind becomes preoccupied with itself and your own interests, likes and dislikes, theories and experiences. Your ability to empathize lessens greatly and you find yourself easily irritated and avoiding people who do not share the same mindset as yours (practically the rest of the world). You've become so used to expending energy inwards that it becomes a Herculean effort to try and get to know others. You'd rather not pretend to be glad about Megan's new boyfriend (who sounds like a piece of s**t) or grudgingly compliment Billy on his decision to take his kids to Disneyland rather than pay off his arrears for the car or be pressured into attending the church cake sale when you're secretly an atheist. Living alone makes you that person who just doesn't want to make that effort to get to know the people around you. Getting to know people seems about as difficult and exhausting as someone with physique of Gandhi trying to do the workout of a prime Arnold Schwarzenegger. Unless you are a natural recluse, living alone is not a good idea for the reasons stated above. But hey that's just my two cents.

Did you ever stop caring about how old you are? I remember when I was 17 and the anxiety I felt knowing that in a few months I would be a full fledged adult with responsibilities. Ripe for work life, going steady and potential marriage. Reality: I was just a kid still going to school and nothing remotely resembling a girlfriend. I remember when I was 19 how much the prospect of turning 20 meant. The big 2–0 meant that I was a ‘hardback’ man planning his career, house and family. No time for shits and giggles. Reality: This was the most immature period of my life and I was far from any kind of career, house or family. I had more time than ever for shits and giggles. I remember at 25 I observed my hairline beginning to recede. I was paranoid that I was going bald. I felt like I would be seen as a balding old perv if I chatted up 18 yo girls in the mall. I thought I was no longer a youth. Reality: I was not a balding old perv but a young man with self esteem issues. At 30 I was working two jobs trying to make ends meet. I had a daughter and was in a troubled relationship with her mother. The last thing I cared about was how old I was and I haven’t put much thought to it since almost seven years later. The moral of my story is I would’ve enjoyed my life much better if I didn’t worry about age and age expectations the way I did as a youth. I am much less bothered about turning 40 than when I was about to turn 20. When the time comes I’ll be proud to know that I was lucky to live so long.

Can you name an actor who was never a good actor but became one? Sterling Hayden never wanted to be an actor. He was coaxed into the profession as a young, handsome sailor whose photogenic good looks appealed to a post WWII audience who were just begging for actors who were the image of tall and rugged manliness. The 6′5 blonde, athletic young shipmate got into the industry after a 1938 photo gained popularity in a fisherman's magazine. Dubbed by Paramount as 'The Beautiful Blond Viking God’ he got into the industry as a means to purchase his own ship but grew to resent Hollywood. His early roles were a slew of rather forgettable Westerns and film noirs. After his role in the classic Western Johnny Guitar starring Joan Crawford he became a bonafide star. However around this time his personal life got more attention as he was reported to have communist sympathies during the McCarthy/Red Scare era and during a vicious custody battle for his children he took his four children on a self manned trip aboard his ship Wanderer from San Francisco Bay to Tahiti despite the legal implications that awaited him at home. His impulsive nature, hatred of Hollywood,anti- capitalism sentiments and sometimes reckless behaviour gave him the image of an eccentric, of which is well documented in his autobiography Wanderer (1963). However upon working with Stanley Kubrick in The Killing he found his niche playing manic and impulsive characters, not far removed from his actual personality. His best role arguably being that of the insane American General Jack D. Ripper in Kubrick's classic black political comedy Dr. Strangelove. His final great role was that of corrupt Irish police Captain Mark McCluskey in The Godfather (1972). Despite the critical and commercial resurgence his roles and his writings were used solely to fund his travels of which (along with legal expenses and taxes) he continuously saw his money decrease. He died of prostate cancer at the of 70 in 1986, leaving behind six children.

What are some of the biggest casting blunders in Hollywood movies? I know I may be in the minority with this opinion but when I saw that this guy would be cast as Peter Parker in the first major studio Spiderman movie, disappointment is not strong enough of a word to describe how I felt. Tobey Maguire does not have the wit, charisma and charm of a traditional Peter Parker. Not only that, Maguire was too old for the role from the very first movie. When I saw 27 year old Maguire walking about high school with a jacket, book bag and a distinct 5 o’clock shadow on his face I was immediately taken out of the movie. (Yeah that's definitely a teenaged schoolboy boarding a bus and not a smirking, semi-creepy man pushing 30) Peter Parker is a charming and witty young man, loyal to friends and family, a great problem solver and a smartass with a touch of geekiness. The only characteristic Tobey Maguire demonstrated from the above was the geekiness, of which he laid on as thick as cheesecake. Maguire’s Spiderman was this awkward, pitiable schmuck who had as much charisma and charm as a mild-mannered peeping tom. The whole shtick the producers seemed to go with was to make Peter Parker nothing but a sad, bullied nerd because I guess maybe they arrogantly believed Spiderman fans are nothing but a bunch of nerds who love the comic book not because of its quality story and characters but because it supports a geek fantasy of getting fantastic superpowers through simple means, getting to beat up thugs and bullies and winning chicks. Sam Raimi’s Spiderman targeted that niche when they gave us the whimpering, sensitive, thin-lipped Tobey Maguire as Peter Parker in my honest opinion. Maybe that's my personal opinion but personality aside, Maguire doesn't even have the physical attributes. Spiderman/Parker is 5′10, late teens-early 20s, lean, long-limbed, sinewy and with a head of thick brunette hair. He basically has to have the physique of a well experienced trapeze artist due to all the climbing and swinging Spiderman does. At his best in the film Tobey Maguire was a short limbed and somewhat stocky man measuring somewhere between 5′7 and 5′8 with a crop of thin hair above his smirking, punchable face. I grew up watching Spiderman cartoons and gaining a familiarity with Parker's smart, resonating and confident tone. Maguire's whiny, eerily pubescent voice gave a measure of cringe and creepiness. I am not a fan of Tobey Maguire's Peter Parker and will hold that view for the rest of my life. Andrew Garfield and Tom Holland may not be the gold standard either but they are a lot more closer to the mark. Here's hoping that they get it right the next movie.

Have you ever walked out of a movie theater early over a feature movie that you simply could not continue to sit through? If so, what was the movie? To this day there is only one movie that was so detestable that I couldn't even sit through it halfway. This movie took all the absolute worst aspects of popular 2010s rom-coms and sex-coms and moulded it into one smelly ball and held it under my my nose for a gruelling 40 minutes. Honestly I've seen many rom-coms and sex-coms that I know to be silly and over-the-top but they manage to provide a level of entertainment. Good writers manage to insert a few relatable scenes and characters that keep it from straying into a fairytale. Also a good writer would understand that good-humour and charm is necessary for a rom-coms and sex-coms to be enjoyable. There is nothing remotely good-humoured about Love and Other Drugs (2010). No one is charming. Everyone is a foulmouth, nihilist/narcissist. The very premise of the story is dark and ugly. A rising pharmaceutical salesman gets romantically involved with one of his customers whose health deteriorates whilst his sales increase. Will he learn the value of love can't bought with all the cash in the world? Will he learn that pharmaceuticals are to help people and not to get rich off of? Will he manage to enjoy a whole bunch of sex with various women while thinking of the above? The movie is infuriating because it seems to be written by three completely different writers who battled as towards the direction of the movie and time ran out on them. Hate is not a word that I use a lot but this is a movie that I honestly hate. It's a cynical, tasteless movie devoid of any charm that becomes shallower the more it tries to look deep.

Who is the most underestimated horror movie villain? Practically every boy who grew up in the 90s watching horror movies on SyFy (then Sci-Fi) knew of this guy. I'm pretty certain he's responsible for a lot of nightmares we had back then. Revok from David Cronenberg’s sci-fi/body-horror cult classic Scanners (1981) puts a capital V in Villain. He's a powerful, ruthless and deranged psychic (scanner) bent on taking over the world with powers that can control minds and inflict severe physical damage on others. Michael Ironside who portrays Revok is nothing short of excellence. He makes Jack Nicholson’s Joker look like Mr. Rogers with his intense facial expressions, sinister grimacing and lip curling as well as his menacingly emotionless voice. No one can forget the famous scene at the beginning of the movie where Revok calmly and sarcastically pretends to be ‘scanned’ by a weaker fellow scanner only to casually cause the man's head to explode within seconds. Few actors can put such a stamp on a performance like Ironside did as he did with Revok. Scanners may be a bit of a forgotten movie by now but no one can ever forget the character Revok and Ironside's performance.

Have you ever met a dangerous person and not known it at the time? Maurice was a soft-spoken and mild mannered boy in my class. He was friendly and pleasant to all. I cannot think of a single moment where he said or did something that angered or offended anyone while in school. He lived further up the hill from where my school was; practically walking distance from the school. Girls confided in him due to his reserved nature and boys respected his kindness. Once he invited a few of us guys to his house for food and to watch SpiderMan (the very first movie) on his PC, after school. Maurice was the last boy one would think of when the word ‘dangerous’ was mentioned. When we entered Form 5, a boy named Kevin entered the school and stoke fear upon many of us. I say ‘boy’ but he was already an 18yo adult when he came. He had transferred from a really rough school and practically every week he was involved in vicious fights or would be seen breaking class to smoke behind the labs. He would harass random boys, threaten them for their money and if they didn't cough up he'd shove, slap or thrash them, according to his mood. Maurice happened to pass by him one day and judging Maurice to be harmless he tackled Maurice for some money. Maurice ignored him but Kevin grabbed him by the shirt and slapped him on both cheeks, warning him that next time things will be worse. Maurice's shirt was dirty and his face red from the fracas but he remained silent and walked away. After school ended I was walking with my friends out the compound and down the hill when we saw trouble was brewing. We saw a gang of no less than twenty young men from the area had accosted Kevin. Kevin's face was bruised and swollen, eyes red and most of his shirt buttons were ripped out from a prior struggle. They dragged Kevin to Maurice and asked what to do with him. Maurice, in his soft voice told them that that was enough. The men shoved Kevin off and fired kicks behind him as he ran down the hill, thoroughly learning his lesson. The hill where the school lay was Maurice's turf. Kevin learned a lesson that day. The most dangerous people are sometimes the ones you least suspect.

What is the most obnoxious type of student for a teacher? I'm not a teacher, but my job requires teaching random subjects to the younger students for a single period a day. In my many years of doing this I've always noticed a trend. Let's pretend this is a class clown. He (let's be honest, most of the time it's a boy) has self esteem issues and believes that the only way his peers can recognize his existence is by drawing attention to himself by disrupting the class with jokes, pranks or just acting as stupid as humanly possible. The class clown is NOT the most obnoxious type of student. These are the students who always laugh at and encourage the class clown, regardless of how unfunny/disruptive his performance. These are the fake audience. They are by far the most obnoxious students in a class. In my experience class clowns tend to go through a phase. Most of them grow out of their clownish behaviours as they get older and many of them actually prove themselves to be thoughtful, intelligent and caring. The fake audience (which usually comprises under 5 students) are the one who are real disruptors of the class. They are the ones who are truly inconsiderate and disrespectful. They usually have a consistently bad attitude. They manipulate the class clown to disrupt the class by providing an audience. This allows for them to channel their defiance and disrespect towards you by using a hapless class clown surrogate. When the giggles have ended and the majority of the class have decided to get serious, the fake audience will urge Mr. Clown to continue his antics. Regardless of how unfunny and irritating the clown's later performance is, they hold their bellies in false laughter in a effort to give rise to anarchy and poor Mr. Clown is held fully responsible and gets in serious trouble. The sad fact is the fake audience, in many cases, do not even like the class clown and have nothing to do with him outside of class. My trick for dealing with class clown disruptions is that I totally ignore him. Instead I concentrate on spotting the fake audience members who are egging him on. I then point them out and bring them to the front of the class, letting them know that they are in trouble for disrupting the class and will be taken to the Principal or Safety Officer's office. Like clockwork this action usually follows. The highlighted fake audience becomes enraged and demonstrate overwhelming disrespect, arguing with me that the class clown is the one who disrupted the class and they are innocent. In a short period of time they reveal themselves for who they are by speaking ill against the clown, they start passionately arguing their rights, some go as far as making threats, some walk out of the class and some point the blame at one another. All in all they reveal themselves to the class (and the class clown) what disrespectful, manipulative, conceited and resentful little creatures they are. Works every time. Edit 5.05.22. What are some dirty tactics used by fast food restaurants? I worked delivery for a popular local pizzeria in Trinidad for some years and left somewhat dishonorably discharged after having arguments with management over a growing reliance on a dirty, illegal tactic that they employed with no discretion. I can best describe it by means of a short skit. Customer: Hi. Good day. Do you have any specials today? Newly Employed Cashier: Good day. Our Monday special is two large pizzas for only $100. Customer: That's great. That's like two for the price of one. I'll have it. Newly Employed Cashier: Yes. We have a different specials everyday. You can check them online or simply ask us. Customer: I appreciate. Great service. The Manager is in the background keenly observing the proceedings. After the customer leaves she approaches the cashier. Manager: Did you just sell that man two pizzas for $100? Newly Employed Cashier: Uh...yeah...the special? Manager: So you sold just the two pizza special? What about the donuts and cookies that we’ll have to discard this evening? What about the salad? I need you to sell all of these before the end of the day. Newly Employed Cashier: I'm trying but most people just want the two pizzas for $100 special. Manager: This branch doesn’t have a two pizzas for $100 special. Our special is two pizzas, four donuts, four cookies and a salad for $160. Newly Employed Cashier: But that's not what we have advertised. What if….. Manager: What if we have this discussion about this in Head Office tomorrow? A new customer walks in with his wife and two children and approaches the cashier. Customer 2: Hi. I heard you guys have some kind of special for two pizzas? The cashier glances at the Manager staring at her. Newly Employed Cashier: Yes. Two pizzas, four donuts, four cookies and a salad for $160. Customer 2: Okay. I really don't want all that other stuff. I could've sworn I saw online it was just two pizzas for the price of one….? He stares intently at the cashier and hoping for her to give him the offer he wanted. His wife then urges him to take the offer as the kids are getting restless. The customer grudgingly accepts. The customer behind him is well dressed in a suit and is discussing a legal matter with a client on his cell phone. Customer 3: Hi. I'll have the two pizza special. One pepperoni, the other veggie. Newly Employed Cashier: The special today is two pizzas with four donuts… She feels a nudge on her arm. The Manager is motioning for her to shut up. The Manager enters the order just as the customer asked. The customer takes his bill and moves away. Manager: I'm going to spend the rest of the day giving you additional training in sales. You need to know how to sell and who to sell.

Which kind of news do you like to access? Why? Anything that is relevant to my way of life and personal interests. It sounds selfish but it's the truth. In the school where I work I teach children the art of how to read the newspaper. Random citizen over 40: 'How to read the newspaper?!’ What?! Children must get in the habit of reading the entire newspaper……every day……front to back…..all the time. Otherwise they will be ignorant.’ To that idealistic but naive person I would reply no. The paradox of modern life is that the more time we spend viewing the news, the more uncritical we allow ourselves get henceforth the more dumb we get. If I lived my life according to the news today I'd think that: Growing up in Trinidad we are taught to listen to the news, not follow it. Because of our colonial past as a tiny island with a large grapevine network, we have had defiance and skepticism over the higher order injected into our bloodstream. ‘Massa say it against the law to trespass into his hunting ground…’ ‘Massa say all trespassers will be shot…' ‘Pahgo say that Massa gone with he family to live in Scotland. Don't even care about hunting ground....does come back to estate only once a year…' ‘I going into the hunting ground…’ Regardless of the critical thinking aspect, I tell students the worst thing to do a newspaper is read it from the front page to the back. It's just such a waste of time to read the newspaper/listen to the news programs in its entirety. The average Trinidadian newspaper usually has 100 pages more or less. 50% is usually advertisements. 20% is usually feature sections of mild interest i.e. How Edward overcame his disability to become a firefighter etc etc. 5% is sport 10% is specialized news: business, technology, health etc 5% is opinions and editorials 10% is relevant news that can be related to the average person. Of that 10% relevant Average Joe news only the first paragraph is of interest and more likely than not political slants are applied, data is exaggerated/underrepresented, status quo agendas and biases are applied to such and such. I tell students to spend more time skimming and skipping articles than actually reading the paper. Trinidad is a small country and we have the benefit of getting together in small units and discussing what we heard/saw on the news and filtering what may be truth from what is bulls**t based on our own common sense, trusted sources, scuttlebutt and that beautiful grapevine that we have that has never failed us for centuries. And the beauty of our grapevine style of news is that it doesn't cost a dime in subscription. Just go out into your world and be friendly. You'd pick up on some news relavent to your existence in less than an hour. Just be sure to verify your information with various trusted sources. All hail scuttlebutt. All hail the grapevine.

Have you ever had a co-worker who you worked closely with get fired for something truly shocking that you never saw coming? He was fired. It was shocking. But I personally saw it coming a mile away. So I'm cheating a bit. Sean was a fellow delivery driver at a pizza restaurant. He was the epitome of the go-getting, happy-go-lucky type of guy who always saw the best in everyone around him. In our restaurant (and most fast food restaurants in the country) the staff is overwhelmingly women. As a male employed in a fast-paced female environment, us male delivery drivers knew that you had to be firm and assertive with the female coworkers otherwise they'd take advantage of you. Sean didn't seem to get the cue. He would mop the floors, refill ice bins, sweep, go out and pickup lunch, lift heavy boxes of meat etc for any female who had the ability to remember his name. He loved to make people happy. Us drivers would warn him to stick with his job specs otherwise he'd be doing favours all day and not get any deliveries done. He paid us no heed. One fateful day, the Assistant Manager held a meeting. She noticed for the past few weeks the meat stocks were going missing. Every week she did a quick audit of the remaining stocks and usually the figure would be off by a package or two. However her audit revealed entire cases of meat were vanishing with no possible explanation other than in-house theft. After viewing the security cameras for a lengthy period she finally discovered the culprit. Sean was fired promptly. Everyone was shocked. Nobody expected Sean, with his heart of gold, to be a petty meat thief. Sean passionately declared his innocence. However the camera footage revealed that he kept entering the chiller where meat and other food ingredients were kept. Delivery drivers had no reason to go in the chiller unless it was busy and they were asked to help bring out stock. The footage also revealed Sean exiting the chiller several times with a mysterious bag just before his shift ended. Sean passionately declared his innocence but management would hear nothing of it. He was fired and blacklisted from ever working at any of the branches again. However meat still continued to go missing at an alarming rate. The assistant manager was at her wits end trying to solve the mystery. The head office warned that any further loss of meat stocks would be deducted from everyone's salary. These were the magic words that made everyone on the alert for the thief. In a few days a breakthrough came when one of the workers confided to the manager that one of the newer workers (I'll refer to her as Janet) kept bringing lunch and putting it in the chiller. However Janet would never be seen eating the lunch that she brought. Instead she would always return the bag home. This was indeed suspicious. Upon inspecting Janet's lunch bag they found a pack of ham. Janet was the culprit all along. She admitted to her crime and with the threat of criminal proceedings, management got her to confess that Sean was innocent. She admitted that Sean had a crush on her and would give her a ride home when both of their shifts ended the same time. Before they left she would ask that he retrieve her 'lunch’ from the chiller for her. Sean never suspected a thing and innocently and unwittingly assisted in her theft. Feeling guilty the assistant manager called Sean to ask if he wanted his job back. Sean declined the offer. He had gotten a much more lucrative position working for a cable company as a technician. Had he still been working at the restaurant he wouldn't have known that they were hiring. Some things happen for the best. I was very happy for Sean. Unfortunately for us we were no longer allowed to keep our lunches in the chiller from the that moment on.

He was not all that gifted intellect-wise and there was even a time when he begged me (the top performing student in class) to allow him to beat me in exams so he could get top grades and get the Sega Genesis his parents promised upon achieving such a feat. I was a vain bastard and didn't let that happen for him. Fast forward twenty years later and I'm walking through the streets of San Juan, trying to flag a taxi to get to a job interview for a much needed part time delivery job, I see a sexy electric blue Impreza pull up next to me. The windows slide down and I see it's my old friend Mitra who I hadn't seen in decades. He gives me a heartfelt shake of the hand and with absolutely no trace of conceit he explains to me that he has a thriving car-parts business/garage. Upon looking him up on Facebook I find out that along with his parents' old home in Trinidad he has a house in Hennessy, Oklahoma. Yes. The guy who I wouldn't let beat me in final exams got the last laugh and with dividends to boot. Couldn't happen to a nicer guy though. Feel free to check out his business here.

What annoys you about people your age? People my age (37) are in the middle aged category and tend to be very sensitive when discussing their career, life goals and personal lives. It may just be me but I’ve noticed that most people here in their mid 30’s - early 40s tend to be more private about themselves and their personal lives and they are a lot more risk averse. I’ve observed passive aggressiveness more common among people my age (35 - 44) than in any other age group. In my experience in workplace settings I’ve also noticed that brown-nosing, bad workaholic tendencies, exploitative/manipulative behavior, micromanaging etc comes more from people my age and rarely from those in young or older categories. What was your mechanic scam that you caught that they never expected you to find? Some mechanics will charge you based on how you look/dress. Not a scam but rather a form of stereotyping. For a period in my life I worked two jobs. During the day I had an office job in a Ministry in the Government and during the evening I worked pizza delivery. I drove a beat-up, old pickup that was over twenty years old and looked it. At some point in time I was badly overdue in terms of an oil change. I had a decent mechanic, Doc, who would not only change my oil but also my air, fuel and oil filters AND fix any minor issues that needed attention. For all this he would charge $150 TT ($21 US). This was an exceptionally good rate compared to the price and quality of service I got from all the other mechanics. Sadly, Doc began having health problems and I was forced to look for a new mechanic. I was informed of a father-son mechanic team who were known for great service and affordable rates. I took some time off my office job and headed towards their location probably looking a lot like this: I was in some of my best threads, sporting a new haircut and pair of glasses, full of confidence and dare I say, looking quite dashing. I did not intend to impress the mechanics, I was not even aware of how I looked. I was simply having a good fashion day. I introduced myself to the mechanics and explained my situation. I gave it my all to be as friendly, polite and sociable as I could and even offered to help bring over tools for them as they worked on my vehicle. During all this time I couldn't help but notice they were being rigidly formal and courteous with me, constantly referring to me as ‘sir,’ avoiding idle chatter and not showing any particular interest in me or my background. When they were finished, I went to the father mechanic and queried the cost. I was expecting $200 at most, maybe even as high as $250 seeing that they finished my job so speedily. However when I heard him nonchalantly mutter $500, my jaw dropped. ‘Five Hundred?!’ I cried, ‘How come so much?’ ‘We changed your oil, the air, fuel and oil filters,’ he explained lifelessly, ‘Aired your tires and eh…changed your gearbox and differential oil……that’s full service.’ ‘I didn’t want full service,’ I cried, ‘I just wanted my oil and filters changed.’ ‘Oil and filters changed?’ he replied almost stupidly, ‘That’s full service. Full service is $500. Isn’t that right Jason?’ He directed that question to his son who was in the process of jacking up someone’s car. ‘Yup,’ Jason replied monotonously without glancing, ‘Ask anybody here.’ There was a silence. I realized there was nothing I could do. I should’ve queried the cost before I allowed them to work on my pickup. I paid them their money and left, feeling thoroughly cheated and irritated, telling myself I would never do business with them again. Some weeks later I’m off to start my shift doing pizza delivery on a busy Friday evening. I’m nowhere near looking my best as I’m sporting a washed out and stained ‘Mario’s Pizza’ shirt, a beaten up red cap, a baggy and threadbare trousers and I’m in dire need of a haircut. My appearance was similar to the photo below but far more scruffy. I pressed on the clutch pedal, only to find that it was slow to rise up from the floor. Clearly my clutch had a bad fluid leak. If my vehicle broke down I would have to pay a fortune to hire a wrecker and quite possibly miss my shift. I saw that I wasn’t far from the father and son garage so I slowly guided the pickup into their compound. They saw me looking frantic and disheveled in my old pizza delivery clothes and immediately came to my assistance. I cut the pleasantries short and informed them of the clutch problem and how my manager would ‘have my ass if I took a day off on a Friday.’ They told me to calm down, that it wasn’t a serious matter. They began to jokingly tease me that they wouldn’t work on my pickup unless I brought a free pizza for them. They then proceeded to engage in idle chatter regarding fast food vs home cooked meals as they jacked up the pickup and put it on stands. I then realized that they didn’t recognize me with this shoddy uniform. They looked so much at ease and were so much friendlier than when I last visited them. Then the son got into his car, drove off and returned with a clutch slave cylinder and fluid and in two-twos they had my pickup back in order. I was quite impressed and grateful for the speedy service. However I cringed knowing that I would probably be slapped another $500 fee. I queried to the father mechanic as to how much my bill was and he said to his son, ‘How much you pay for that stuff Jason?’ ‘About two hundred,’ Jason replied. ‘Give us $250 pizza man. It’s your lucky day. Just make sure and bring us a pizza when you get the chance.’ ‘Of course!’ I lied. They barely charged for the labor. In fact they were much more fond of me as a salt-of-the-Earth, minimum wage earning, slave to the customer, regular Joe, plying his trade to make a living. They saw me as one of their own and extended a helping hand to someone who they believed roughed it out in life. Had they known that this was actually my second job and I had a comfortable office job in a Government Ministry, I would’ve seen a much different outcome. So I learned a decent hack in life when dealing with mechanics and various other tradesmen. I don’t work pizza delivery anymore but whenever I go to see those mechanics or go to meet plumbers, electricians, builders etc, I wear that old Mario’s Pizza uniform to counteract against their built in stereotypes. Doing this I find myself getting good rates, great service and making new friends much better than if I were wearing office wear and a fancy tie. C’est la vie! Edit 10.01.22. Those mechanics tend to scheme but you can find a way around them. They pale in comparison to the illegal scams some of our fast food restaurants attempt on a daily basis. Why does the Caribbean island of Dominica get so few tourists? This may be pretty assumptive but Dominica is like an archaic little town on a little island, surrounded by mountains, surrounded by banana trees and surrounded by real, 100% indigenous Carib tribe Amerindians (Native Americans). Indigenous (Carib) teenaged girls selling souvenirs. (I was told they were superstitious against having their pictures taken, but managed to sneak this one behind them.) The first thing one would notice once they arrive at the capital Roseau is that they are transported back into the early 19th century. All the buildings of colonial days are there and still intact. One can see the architectural styles of the Spanish, French, English and even Irish in the building facades. There are some quite interesting architectural innovations to discover when you go to more rural locations. The people that I met were very friendly and laid back. I may get some flak for this but to me the Dominican accent can be best described as a Nigerian trying to sound French or Haitian trying to speak English. Go to the market at Roseau early on a Sunday morning and you will hear the Dominican brogue in all its glory. The group I went with unanimously found their accent and sing song very charming albeit amusing. The locals in turn found my accent strange and asked if I came from India. If you look at this basic map you would notice that Dominica is populated mostly at the coasts. If England is known for its fields Dominica should definitely be known for its mountains. The stocky mountains there stretch as far as the eye can see. It gives one a surreal feeling when driving towards higher altitudes. The hotel we stayed in was called La Flamboyant. When I heard the name I just figured it was just another generic, pseudo-exotic hotel name. However when we got there, the sensation of nails on a chalkboard was felt in my eyes. Yes. Somebody thought it was a good idea to paint a very dreary, blocky building in the most garish and loud colours of the kaleidoscope. If the question is why Dominica lacks tourists, maybe it's because they saw La Flamboyant while looking for hotels online. Funny Story As a very amateur fisherman, I spent a day fishing with a primitive caster and using beef liver as bait. The local fisherman laughed at me and subtly complained in their barely discernable patois that I was stinking up the place and attracting flies with my bloody beef liver. The problem was I didn't come with enough EC dollars to buy proper bait and beef liver was cheapest meat I could buy that would hold well on a hook. After an hour of no success I felt my line pull and the fishermen watched in amazement as I pulled up the most hideous sea creature I ever witnessed in my life. I am so sorry I didn't have the nerve to take a proper video to capture this creature in all its sheer horror. The fishermen around me ran off in fear as the creature looked like it would chase after them on its legs. I myself was severely tempted to throw it back in the water with caster hook and line. Hell, even throw my remaining beef liver behind it to appease its wrath. I flung it back in the water and severed the line with my knife. The creature, now uglier sporting an emo-style lip piercing, swam away in a very unsettling, human like manner. I learned later that this was called a Batfish. When the fishermen returned, I showed them the photos and they chastised me for not getting a bucket and keeping it. They said they would’ve used it as a tourist attraction. Hence, reason #2 Dominica has scarce tourists: I didn't get a bucket to keep the Batfish. On a sidenote, Dominica specializes in two resources: Bananas and souvenirs. Every nook and cranny you will see either a banana tree or someone selling souvenirs under a tent/umbrella. Try to buy from the ones who do not have conveniently located stalls as we noticed that amongst the several dozens of souvenir stalls in Roseau, only a handful actually get significant sales. Also, be aware that most of the souvenirs are not handcrafted by local artisans as they tend to claim. Nearly all of them seem to be imported from China. (The Caribs are masters of pretending to be the artisans of their wares). They put a big Dominica sticker to cover the 'Made in China’ engraving. So to answer the question seriously, why Dominica lacks tourism. The answer is simple. They aren't Westernized enough to attract the typical tourist. Don't expect to see a KFC next to a McDonald's or a big sprawling Ibiza style nightclub next to a Holiday Inn. They are an ecotourism style country and attract tourists who appreciate the purity and serenity of a land lost in time.

How would you handle an employee who refuses to attend company parties? I am such an employee. Imagine your company’s yearly Christmas party going from something like this: To this: And no. It has nothing to do with COVID restrictions. For years, the biggest pizza chain in the country stopped allocating a day for the annual Christmas party. This party was the company’s best demonstration of appreciation to its dedicated staff. The company would book a spot in a fancy hotel and all staff members would be invited to have an evening to dress in their best and wine, dine and dance the night away. With new upper management at the helm (the founder’s son) this was seen as an unnecessary expense. Instead it was decided to send some money to each store manager whom would be entrusted to host a decent Christmas party for staff. This allowed for the worst slap-in-the-face Christmas party that one could ever imagine: As would be expected, many hated the new Christmas party but there was a fear of being blacklisted and victimized by the manager if you didn’t attend. There was no transparency as to how much money the manager received from the Head Office and what he/she spent it (and your additional $100) on. Can you provide some examples of average actors delivering great performances due to well-written characters? Let's be frank. Samuel L. Jackson is a one trick pony. But gosh darn it that sure is one hell of a trick that motherf****n pony does. All jokes aside I find it hard to think of Quintin Tarantino writing the character Jules without envisioning Samuel L. Jackson in mind for the role in Pulp Fiction. It is truly the role Jackson was born to play. It is the role that took Jackson into stardom and to this day Jules’ intimidating obscenity ridden threats, interrogation, debates on burgers and pork, not to mention his love of quoting Ezekiel 25:17 is constantly memed, quoted and parodied. But I wouldn't consider Jackson a great actor. He may sit more comfortable with his tough guy roles but he isn't anywhere near the range of other legendary tough guy actors like Denzel Washington, Clint Eastwood and James Cagney. If you know Jackson is going to be in a movie you are certain that he isn't going to be a bespectacled data programmer hunched behind a computer or a main love interest. He is probably the most famous typecast of Hollywood film history since John Wayne. It's a bit unfortunate because when he attempts more vulnerable or intellectual characters it comes across as forgettable at best and eerie at worst in my honest opinion (Tarzan, RoboCop, Star Wars). I don't think Sam may get another role as defining and well written as Jules in Pulp Fiction. I think a large portion of his filmography isn't impressive from an acting standpoint. He may not be a Marlon Brando or a Laurence Olivier but neither of them could've put in the heart and energy into an intricately moulded character such as Jules Winnfield.

What screams "I make terrible financial decisions!"? I worked with a lady in her early 40s at a pizza restaurant. She was just a ordinary grunt like the rest of us. She aspired to be a supervisor but what held her back was that she had 6 kids, three, in their late teens/early adulthood for one father, another two of toddler age for another father and a baby for her recent boyfriend. This domestic situation made it hard for her punctuality and regularity at work as there was always a babysitting issue or child maintenance issue that needed resolving with her two exes. Her current boyfriend was no supportive stalwart himself as practically once every week she would stop her duties to go outside the restaurant to have long and intense arguments with him on the phone in regards to his inability to come pick her up that evening or various other disagreements that they had. In person the boyfriend had a nasty, arrogant attitude and seemed to care only for casual sex, his car and for her to keep his baby away from her older kids whom they all shared a mutual dislike with one another. She lived with her two toddlers and her baby at her father's house which was shared with several other siblings of similar circumstance. With that there was a lot of family fighting in regards to space and ownership. To put it bluntly she lived in a world of shit. Given the circumstances it seemed unlikely that she would be unable break free from the poverty and drudgery any time soon. I would feel the greatest sympathy for her and try my best to help her at work in any regards. That is until that fateful day when I saw her rubbing her stomach and smiling to herself. ‘Looks like you're ready for another one (baby)’ I said jokingly. She smiled and said that she and her current boyfriend (the arrogant dickhead) was trying for another baby. They had a girl and now he wanted a boy. ‘Are you serious?’ I said. I was flabbergasted that she was saying this so casually. It was as if she suddenly reverted back to a naive 16 yr old who found her first love and was no longer a middle aged woman with 6 children and a truckload of problems. One of my biggest flaws is that sometimes I can't keep my opinions to myself. ‘But you have 6 kids already!’ For a second she came out of her dream and reverted back to reality. She glared at me angrily for a split second .Then she returned to her child like persona and replied, ‘Children are a blessing.’ ‘Children are a blessing when you can afford to raise them right and give them the love and attention they need.’ Those words just came out of me in very emphatic tone. As a father of one (I worked part time at the restaurant) I was struggling to survive, working two jobs to ensure that my daughter had a future and to ensure all of my free time was dedicated to her. This lady worked one job and was dependent on family, friends and the Government to assist with any shortcomings she encountered, which seemed to be every day. I could not relate at all to what she was saying. She glared at me again and the conversation ended. An hour later I'm called into the manager's office. Apparently she got so angry she complained to the manager that I was being emotionally abusive, chauvinistic (the restaurant was 90% female staff) and stuck my nose in other people's business. She even told the manager that my words were so hurtful she felt overcome with hurt that she was considering taking a sick day and leaving. I sat and nodded in silence. I was the given a warning and sent out of the office. I learned a sad but valuable lesson that day: Some people are simply destined for a life of hardship and misery through their own stubborn mentality and poor choices. So to answer the question What screams "I make terrible financial decisions!"?: People who get offended by the truth.
